---AGENTS---
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable first-person Three.js web game from the user’s concept: fly a helicopter, shoot giant city-destroying kaiju below, upgrade weapons, and fight flying creatures.

## Requirements
- First-person helicopter gameplay with giant kaiju destroying a city.
- Weapon upgrade system between waves.
- Flying enemy creatures in addition to ground kaiju.
- Mobile/touch support per project conventions.
- Visual quality should be polished and complete.

## Decisions
- Built as a Vite + Three.js static game, titled “ROTOR//TITAN”.
- Procedural low-poly city, kaiju, wyverns, effects, and Web Audio synthesis; no external 3D assets.
- Game loop: waves of kaiju + flyers, city integrity and hull health, score/combo, upgrades after each wave, game-over/retry.
- Desktop controls: mouse aim, LMB Vulcan, RMB missiles, WASD flight, R/F altitude, Shift boost, Esc pause.
- Mobile: virtual joystick, drag-to-look, fire/missile/altitude buttons.
- Retry/menu uses page reload with `sessionStorage` flag for auto-redeploy to guarantee a fresh destructible city.

## Work State

### Completed
- Created all core game code and UI.
- Implemented procedural city with window textures, roads, traffic, skyline, sky shader, lighting, smoke/particles, debris, explosions, searchlights.
- Implemented player helicopter cockpit, flight physics, camera shake, Vulcan hitscan, heat/overheat, missiles, target lock, radar, HUD.
- Implemented kaiju and flying wyvern models, animation, AI, attacks, death effects.
- Implemented wave spawning, city damage, scoring/combos, upgrades, pause, game over, menu/briefing.
- Added responsive CSS and mobile controls.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Dev server running in tmux session `rotor` on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser installed and screenshot script exists at `/tmp/opencode/shot.mjs`.

### Active
- Visual debugging/testing. First screenshot attempt produced severe WebGL shader/context errors and a likely broken frame (`screenshots/menu-01.png` was still written).

### Blocked
- Screenshot capture under SwiftShader: initial `playwright-cli screenshot` hit a 5s timeout; custom Playwright script emitted repeated `THREE.WebGLProgram: Shader Error ... VALIDATE_STATUS false` and `WebGLRenderer: Context Lost/Restored`, likely due to SwiftShader pressure or shader compilation issue. Need inspect screenshot and optimize/fix.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/menu-01.png` to see whether rendering is usable despite context errors.
2. Reproduce with lower resolution / reduced scene cost; check whether errors are SwiftShader-specific or an actual shader/program issue.
3. Reduce heavy costs if needed: shadow map 2048 → 1024/off, pixel ratio, mesh count, particle counts, remove/disable unsupported shader paths.
4. Re-test menu screenshot, then click Deploy and capture gameplay/cockpit/kaiju screenshots.
5. Validate gameplay interactions: start, pointer lock/drag aim, shooting, missile lock, kills, wave clear, upgrade cards, deploy next wave, pause, game over, mobile layout.
6. Fix any runtime/gameplay bugs found, including `player.lastDamageAt` handling and visual composition.
7. Optimize font imports to Latin-only to shrink build.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: all menu, HUD, upgrade, pause, game-over DOM.
- `src/main.js`: game orchestrator, state machine, wave/combat logic, menu camera, input/UI wiring.
- `src/player.js`: flight controller, camera, cockpit integration, Vulcan/missile/heat logic.
- `src/entities.js`: Kaiju and Flyer procedural models, animation, AI.
- `src/world.js`: procedural city, sky, lights, buildings, traffic, destruction.
- `src/effects.js`: particle systems, tracers, explosions, debris.
- `src/cockpit.js`: first-person cockpit and instrument screens.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, radar, target lock, upgrades, banners, game-over UI.
- `src/projectiles.js`: player missiles and enemy plasma orbs.
- `src/upgrades.js`: upgrade definitions and choice generation.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized engine, weapons, explosions, roar, UI sounds.
- `src/styles.css`: full visual design and responsive/touch layout.
- `screenshots/menu-01.png`: first captured menu render, must be inspected.
- `/tmp/opencode/shot.mjs`: custom Playwright screenshot script with 120s screenshot timeout.

## Important Context
- Working tree changes are uncommitted/untracked.
- Dev server command used: tmux session `rotor`, `npm run dev -- --port 3002`.
- Playwright needs `DISPLAY=:0` and SwiftShader; `playwright-cli` screenshot has a fixed 5s timeout, so use `/tmp/opencode/shot.mjs` for longer captures.
- Custom script usage: `DISPLAY=:0 node /tmp/opencode/shot.mjs http://localhost:3002 screenshots/file.png 1440 900 3000`.
- Build output showed a 599 kB JS chunk and unnecessary Devanagari font subsets; font imports can be narrowed.
- `start.sh` requires `RUNTIME_DIR` and builds/serves via runtime script; Vite dev server is currently used instead.
- No favicon exists; browser console logs a harmless 404 for `/favicon.ico`.
- Potential logic issues to verify: cockpit scene parent wiring, flyer death velocity applied twice, holding fire during wave-clear, camera/aim alignment with shake, and auto-redeploy pointer lock limitations.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a polished, playable first-person Three.js web game: pilot a helicopter, destroy giant city-destroying kaiju below, upgrade weapons between waves, and fight flying creatures.

## Requirements
- First-person helicopter gameplay with giant kaiju attacking a city.
- Weapon upgrade system between waves.
- Flying enemy creatures in addition to ground kaiju.
- Mobile/touch support with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Visual quality should feel complete and polished.

## Decisions
- Vite + Three.js static game titled “ROTOR//TITAN”.
- Everything procedural: low-poly city, kaiju, wyverns, effects, Web Audio; no external 3D assets.
- Game loop: waves of kaiju + flyers, city integrity and hull health, score/combo, upgrades after each wave, game-over/retry.
- Desktop controls: mouse aim, LMB Vulcan, RMB missiles, WASD flight, R/F altitude, Shift boost, Esc pause.
- Mobile: virtual joystick, drag-to-look, fire/missile/altitude buttons; cockpit hidden on touch to maximize view.
- Cockpit kept on desktop; touch HUD compacted for portrait and landscape.
- Retry/menu uses page reload with `sessionStorage` flag for auto-redeploy.

## Work State

### Completed
- All core game code and UI implemented: procedural city, sky, lighting, traffic, fires, kaiju/wyvern models and AI, player flight/physics, Vulcan, missiles, overheat, lock-on, radar, HUD, waves, upgrades, pause, game-over, menu, briefing.
- `npm run build` succeeds; JS chunk ~602 kB, CSS ~43.5 kB. Fonts narrowed to Latin-only subsets.
- Dev server running in tmux session `rotor` at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Screenshot tooling works via `/tmp/opencode/shot3.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/shot4.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/shot-mobile.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/shot-landscape.mjs`.
- Verified menu, gameplay, combat hits, missiles, upgrade card selection, wave 3, pause, game-over, portrait and landscape mobile renders.
- Fixed menu not appearing in screenshots by waiting longer / forcing opacity during capture.
- Fixed upgrade screenshot by directly invoking `_openUpgrade()`; timer-based clear is still valid, just slow under SwiftShader.
- Major visual improvements: scene lighting/fill, stronger window emissives, brighter searchlight, larger kaiju scales matching menu stat, olive/maroon monster colors, slitted orange eyes, subtle internal glow, burning ruins/facade fires and smoke, narrower cockpit side rails.
- Mobile fixes: cockpit hidden on touch, top HUD reflowed, touch controls moved to bottom, compact landscape weapon/flight HUD, landscape menu compacted and no longer clipped.
- Performance safeguards: low-power mode for touch (1024 shadows, fewer embers/skyline, fewer fire lights).

### Active
- Final visual polish and validation of latest changes (kaiju/fire/lighting/mobile CSS edits not yet fully re-screenshot after last tweaks).
- Verify mobile interactions: joystick, drag-to-look, fire, missile, altitude buttons, pause/upgrade responsiveness.
- Validate full wave→upgrade→deploy flow and game-over/retry.

### Blocked
- SwiftShader software rendering runs at ~1–3 fps, making timer-based gameplay transitions take a long real time. Use forced state changes for screenshots; this is not a game bug.

## Next Move
1. Re-run desktop screenshots after latest edits (`searchlight 130`, new menu kaiju at `(16,0,38)`, reduced fire lights) and inspect menu/play/kill.
2. Re-run portrait/landscape mobile screenshots after latest CSS changes and confirm no HUD/control overlap.
3. Run a mobile interaction script to tap/hold touch controls and verify player movement, look, fire, missile, altitude.
4. Test full natural wave clear → upgrade → deploy using forced `game.clearTimer` or direct `_openUpgrade()` if needed.
5. Verify pause/resume and game-over/retry paths, including auto-redeploy.
6. Fix any remaining issues: accuracy can exceed 100% (`player.hits / player.shots` includes missile hits), possible fire sprite visibility, kaiju head/body readability.
7. Final `npm run build` and clean up test artifacts if desired.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: game orchestrator, state machine, wave/combat logic, menu camera, fires, input/UI wiring.
- `src/player.js`: flight controller, searchlight, camera, cockpit integration, Vulcan/missiles/heat.
- `src/entities.js`: Kaiju/Flyer models, scales, materials, AI, death animation.
- `src/world.js`: city generation, lights, ruins, fire sites, destruction, sky.
- `src/effects.js`: particles, tracers, explosions, shockwave rings, debris.
- `src/cockpit.js`: first-person cockpit geometry/instrument screens.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, radar, target lock, upgrades, banners, game-over.
- `src/projectiles.js`: player missiles and enemy plasma orbs.
- `src/upgrades.js`: upgrade definitions and choice generation.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized engine/weapons/explosions/UI sounds.
- `src/styles.css`: full visual design, responsive/touch layouts, landscape menu fix.
- `index.html`: menu, HUD, upgrade, pause, game-over DOM.
- `screenshots/`: latest captures include `v4-menu.png`, `v4-play.png`, `v4-kill.png`, `mobile-portrait-play.png`, `mobile-landscape-play.png`, `mobile-landscape-menu2.png`.
- `/tmp/opencode/shot3.mjs`: full desktop flow capture with forced upgrade.
- `/tmp/opencode/shot4.mjs`: quick desktop menu/play/kill capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/shot-mobile.mjs`: portrait + landscape mobile captures.

## Important Context
- Working tree changes remain uncommitted/untracked; `dist/` exists.
- Dev server command: tmux session `rotor`, `npm run dev -- --port 3002`.
- Playwright needs `DISPLAY=:0`; use custom scripts with longer timeouts instead of `playwright-cli` (fixed 5s).
- WebGL context creation occasionally fails under SwiftShader; retry if `window.__rotorGame` is missing.

- Console shows harmless `/favicon.ico` 404.
- Current start position: `(5, 46, 200)`, pitch `-0.04`; first kaiju spawn at `(0,0,82)`, ~118m away.
